{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2025}}

'''François Proth''' (22 March 1852 &ndash; 21 January 1879) was a self-taught French mathematician and farmer who lived in [[Vaux-devant-Damloup]] near [[Verdun]], [[France]].<ref>{{citation|title=Prime Numbers: The Most Mysterious Figures in Math|first=David|last=Wells|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2011|isbn=9781118045718|page=189|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1MTcYrbTdsUC&pg=PA189}}.</ref>

He stated four primality-related theorems.<ref>{{citation|title=An Introduction to Cryptography|series=Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications|first=Richard A.|last=Mollin|edition=2nd|publisher=CRC Press|year=2010|isbn=9781420011241|page=192|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Vje8TRcLlycC&pg=PA192}}.</ref> The most famous of these, [[Proth's theorem]], can be used to test whether a [[Proth number]] (a number of the form ''k'' × 2<sup>''n''</sup>&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 with ''k'' odd and ''k''&nbsp;<&nbsp;2<sup>''n''</sup>) is prime. The numbers passing this test are called [[Proth prime]]s; they continue to be of importance in the computational search for large prime numbers.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Chaumont | first1 = Alain
 | last2 = Leicht | first2 = Johannes
 | last3 = Müller | first3 = Tom
 | last4 = Reinhart | first4 = Andreas
 | doi = 10.1142/S1793042109002031
 | issue = 2
 | journal = International Journal of Number Theory
 | mr = 2502805
 | pages = 209–218
 | title = The continuing search for large elite primes
 | volume = 5
 | year = 2009}}.</ref>

Proth also formulated [[Gilbreath's conjecture]] on successive differences of primes, 80 years prior to Gilbreath, but his proof of the conjecture turned out to be erroneous.<ref>{{Citation |first=Chris |last=Caldwell |url=http://primes.utm.edu/glossary/page.php?sort=GilbreathsConjecture |title=The Prime Glossary: Gilbreath's conjecture |work=The [[Prime Pages]] }}.</ref>

The cause of Proth's death is not known.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-07-23 |title=10 Non–Rock Stars Who Died at the Tragically Young Age of 27 |url=https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/28318/10-non%E2%80%93rock-stars-who-died-tragically-young-age-27 |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=Mental Floss |language=en-us}}</ref>
